goal: Reproduce the stock TRM Sudoku-Extreme baseline (as-is) to anchor Phase B.

reference.paper: arXiv:2510.04871 (Jolicoeur-Martineau, Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks)

variant: TRM-MLP (attention-free MLP-Mixer; best on Sudoku; no flash-attn required)

arch.recursion_note: H_cycles=T=3, L_cycles=n=6; deep supervision N_sup<=16; single shared 2-layer net; full backprop through the last recursion pass

optim.optimizer: AdamATan2 (pure-PyTorch drop-in, adam_atan2.py — mathematically identical to the fused adam-atan2 kernel; a=1,b=1, decoupled WD)
optim.optimizer_deviation: fused CUDA adam-atan2 unbuildable/unrunnable on sm_120 (torch-header compile error + hardcoded sm_80-90/no-PTX); replaced with an identical-math pure-PyTorch impl. Same accuracy, marginally lower throughput.

train.global_batch_size_deviation: stock is 768 (tuned for 48GB L40S); 768 OOMs on the 32GB RTX 5090 and the harness has no gradient accumulation, so reduced to 512 (largest stable: ~22GB peak, ~9GB headroom). Batch is an accuracy lever, so this may cost a little vs the paper's 87.4%; exact-768 reproduction would need an 80GB card (e.g. Nebius H100).
train.wandb: offline, dirs redirected to /tmp + ~/.cache (cage HOME is read-only); PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True

hardware.flash_attn: not installed (unnecessary for the MLP/Sudoku path)

status: LAUNCHED — stock TRM-MLP baseline training on the 5090 (batch 512, AdamATan2 drop-in); accuracy/throughput to be filled in on completion
